cases.note: Five of seven. `balance` is meaningless on a bolted-down arm, so an IMU bias and a gravity vector are not measurements it is missing — they are measurements it will never take, and reporting them unavailable is a permanent red mark nobody can clear.
All seven. Undeclared capabilities mean nobody said what this body senses, and over-reporting what is missing is the conservative direction.
The absence going the other way: a body that declares capabilities but not a base keeps the two balance sets, because a base nobody described is not a base somebody called fixed.

And the exception to the exception. A body with an IMU keeps both sets whatever its base, since it evidently has one — the fixed-base rule is about what a body cannot do, not about what it has been given.
Three prefixes reach the camera sets and only `sensing.rgb` had ever been written. A depth sensor has intrinsics and extrinsics exactly as an RGB camera does.
The other half of the same `or`: a force sensor earns the F/T bias and the tool offset without any manipulation capability. Only the manipulation side had a case.

One declared capability that reaches none of the sensing rules, on a mobile base: joint zeros and the two balance sets, and no cameras. The case that says `declared` gates the sensing sets rather than the whole table.
